study.question: Why did the complete-row magnitude rule change full-population validation AUC from0.6152795936767026 to0.6149279138846995 on byte-identical source/config replay, while none reproduced0.6151021885074872? Can repeated, identically instrumented magnitude/none runs bracket the earliest observable input, parameter, forward or gradient mismatch beyond the old calls0/512 probes, without changing the frozen training protocol?
study.hypothesis: The historical magnitude advantage is not yet reproducible. A provisional explanation is intervention-sensitive numerical/execution sensitivity, rather than a necessary M17-to-M18 source edit. At shared traced inputs and parameter sketches, magnitude may exhibit nonzero repeated-backward differences and later parameter/forward differences across same-seed runs. Initialization, data order, unobserved histories, optimizer state, environment and checkpoint selection remain alternatives. This is a measurement study, not a new performance mechanism or a diagnosis of GPU nondeterminism.

predictions: If initial learnable states differ, the paired runs show different call0 parameter checksums. This localizes an initialization-state discrepancy, while its origin remains unknown.

If observed static/label prefixes or current supplied batches differ, paired input checksums may first differ at a snapshot. This supports a provided-input/order discrepancy; equal checksums cannot exclude collisions or unsampled history differences.

If checked initial/input signatures agree but parameter signatures first differ between two observed calls, divergence is bracketed to that interval in the traced content. It is not localized to a specific Adam update.

At a sampled identical retained graph, repeated backwards may produce nonzero gradient relative differences/bit sketches. A detected within-state difference supports local numerical variability; the larger question of whether this causes validation drift remains open.

Selective magnitude drift with stable none traces/metrics would be consistent with intervention-sensitive sensitivity; drift in both arms weakens that specificity. Stable traces in both arms leave historical drift unresolved.

Parameter/input sketches agreeing with divergent logits/gradient sketches prioritize a sampled forward/backward audit, subject to collision and unobserved-state limits. A differing selected-checkpoint call count identifies different checkpoint positions, without explaining selection.
No prospective AUC improvement is predicted. Report all four full-population AUCs, losses, signs, costs and original fixed slices; maintain failures and negative evidence.
falsifiers: A mismatch already at call0 parameters or observed input signatures defeats attribution to later magnitude-specific backward behavior without first resolving the mismatch.

Absence of local repeat differences and absence of sampled across-run drift fails to support the proposed numerical-sensitivity explanation in the measured scope; it does not refute unobserved divergence.
Similar none drift prevents treating stable controls as evidence of magnitude specificity. Any source/config difference within a repeated pair invalidates an identical-source contrast.

Any model formula, parameter creation order, optimizer recipe, data/label boundary or frozen setting change invalidates the intended diagnostic comparison. Nonfinite values, more than64 diagnostics, admission failure or cap exhaustion retain failed receipts and suspend attribution.

diagnostic_protocol.comparison_rule: Within each identical-source pair, report exact integer-sketch equality/difference and first observed mismatch, bracketed by the last observed agreement. Different sketches require investigation even with tiny relative errors. Compare only slots captured by both runs; report missing late slots and selected calls rather than substituting zeros.
